pages.title: Licence Warning
pages.text: $(4)$(l)This transmits on a REAL radio.$()$(br2)It links the game's radios to a real rig. $(l)Every$() player who talks through it must hold a real amateur licence and give their own callsign. The server operator is the $(thing)control operator$() and is responsible for all it sends.

pages.title: Both Ways
pages.text: What is said in game on its frequency comes out of the sound card with the real radio keyed (PTT on a serial port's $(thing)RTS$() or $(thing)DTR$() line), and unkeys a moment after.$(br2)What the real radio hears goes on the air in game from the block when its level passes the $(thing)VOX$() threshold, or while its squelch line ($(thing)COS$() on CTS or DSR) is open. A $(thing)time-out timer$(), three minutes by default, drops a transmission that runs too long.

pages.title: Setting It Up
pages.text: It is $(l)off$() until the operator turns on $(thing)real_world_interface_enabled$() and lists the sound cards in $(thing)real_world_interfaces$(), in the server config file only; the comment there explains each setting. $(thing)/radiocraft realworld devices$() lists the names to use.$(br2)The block's screen just picks one of those by name, and shows each device found or not, PTT, VOX/COS and the levels. One block per interface.

pages.title: On the Air
pages.text: In game it is a radio: an antenna on its coax (any band), its frequency, $(thing)FM$() or $(thing)SSB$(), power from the wire. Only operators may change it unless the server allows otherwise.$(br2)$(thing)Everywhere$() needs no antenna and ignores distance: it hears every transmission on its frequency in its dimension, and every station there hears it at full strength. Its traffic is in the moderation log like any other.

pages.title: Your Licence
pages.text: Before your voice goes out through it, click $(thing)I hold an amateur licence$() on its screen. Once is enough, for every interface on the server. Until you do, what you say on the air never reaches the real radio, even through a repeater or in Everywhere mode.$(br2)A quiet $(thing)monitor speaker$() on the block lets those standing by hear what goes out. With the server's op-only setting on (the default), only operators can switch it on or off.
Remember: real licence, real callsign, and identify as the rules require.
